Primary navigation is collapsed behind a "MENU" button even at 1440px, so no part of the site is reachable without a click.
The persistent actions are a phone number (16201) and "Register Interest"; there is no way to browse the project range from the hero.

audience: Two distinct audiences on one page: second-home buyers across its destinations, and equity/IR readers
findings: No <h1> element anywhere on the homepage.
The hero is a five-slide image carousel whose only text is a location label ("Andermatt, Switzerland") — nothing states what the company does or offers.
Body copy renders at 19.6px in mid grey (#666) on white, which is large for body text and low in contrast.
Navigation mixes consumer and investor journeys in a single row: Destinations, Sustainability, Keys Of Life, Investor Relations.
56 images across a 3190px page.
opportunity: Replace the silent carousel with a stated proposition, and separate the buyer path from the investor path.

audience: Cairo homebuyers and investors; Taj City and Sarai are the lead assets
findings: On first load the Next.js route chunk aborted and the browser rendered its own "This page couldn't load" error page. It rendered correctly only after a reload. Reproduced twice; the chunk itself is fetchable, so the failure is in loading rather than availability. NEEDS CONFIRMATION from a normal network.
The <h1> element is present but contains no text.
30 links in the navigation region.
Display type renders at 62px in weight 300 — large but light, so the hierarchy reads softer than its size suggests.
The desktop layout reports negative horizontal overflow (-15px), indicating a scrollbar-width miscalculation.
opportunity: Make the hero render reliably and say something, and cut a 30-link navigation down to the few journeys that matter.
notes: Next.js app router. Custom face monte_regular. Formerly Madinet Nasr for Housing and Development.

audience: Buyers in New Alamein, the New Capital and other NUCA destinations, including overseas Egyptians
findings: No <h1> on the page — the hero headline "Shaping Egypt's Future through Innovative Real Estate Development" is not a heading element.
The hero is a nine-slide carousel ("1 / 9"), so eight of the nine slides are unlikely ever to be seen.
53 images on the page, 7 of them with no alt text.
The strongest content on the page — 6 destinations, 30+ projects, 17,937 homeowners, 12,752 units delivered, 15M sqm, 500+ employees — is confined to a narrow right-hand column.
Floating "Contact us" tab and scroll button overlap the lower-right content.
opportunity: Promote the delivery record and the destination list into the main column, and replace the nine-slide carousel with a deliberate sequence.
notes: EN/AR switcher already present — the Arabic companion face matters more here than elsewhere. Body face AeonikTRIAL, which is a trial licence name and may not be licensed for production. Published hotline 16044.

audience: Domestic and regional leisure guests, plus corporate and event bookers across 20+ Egyptian properties
findings: Two <h1> elements — "Tolip Hotels & Resorts" and "Check Availability".
The hero headline "Feel like a star" is set at 40px on a translucent grey band that clips the text block rather than sitting behind it cleanly.
The hero photograph is a daytime exterior showing the car park, forecourt and building signage, rather than an interior, a room, or a guest experience.
Booking is the business goal, but the hero's only action is "Explore"; "Book Now" is isolated in the top-right corner.
69 images on a 4162px page.
CTA labels are duplicated in the markup and render as repeated text ("Book Now Book Now", "ExploreExplore", "Explore All Explore All").
opportunity: Make availability and booking the hero action, and lead with experience photography instead of building exteriors.
notes: WordPress + Avada/Fusion. Display face Philosopher, body Source Sans Pro. EN/عربي switcher present. Verify the current property list against the live site — several properties moved to Gewan management in 2025.

audience: Overseas travellers and trade partners booking inbound Egypt itineraries; the copy addresses partners as much as consumers
findings: Six <h1> elements, all of them decorative flip-box labels (Leisure Travel, Short Breaks, City Breaks, Leisure Countryside Breaks, Special Events, Corporate Travel), so the page has no heading hierarchy at all.
Navigation is hidden behind a hamburger button at 1440px — zero navigation links are visible on desktop.
Only 3 images on a 6044px page, all three without alt text; most sections are text on flat indigo.
Headings are set all-caps with wide letterspacing at 20px. On mobile the largest heading renders at 15px and body text at 14px, both below the readability floor.
Every call to action is generic — "VIEW MORE", "LEARN MORE", "GET IN TOUCH" — with no stated next step.
opportunity: Build a real hierarchy around the 20-years inbound claim and replace generic buttons with one concrete enquiry action.
notes: WordPress + Elementor with Essential Addons. The only non-property, non-hotel brand on the list alongside GSA, so it carries the most room for a distinct art direction.

audience: Developers and institutional clients commissioning architecture, interiors and urban planning; also course and career applicants
findings: The hero carries no headline — the only text over the opening image is a 16px caption, "SEMA is a cultural and development center located in Qanater El Khayriya, Egypt".
The actual <h1>, "Leading Architecture & Interior Design Firm in Egypt", is set at 36px in weight 400 against 16px body text, so there is almost no scale or weight contrast.
The <title> is keyword-stuffed: "Architecture Firm in Egypt | Architects, Interior Design & Urban Planning | Global Studio Associates".
A social icon rail is pinned over the right edge of the imagery and a chat widget covers the lower-right corner of the viewport.
6595px of page carrying only 7 images, which is thin for a practice whose product is visual.
opportunity: Let the project renders lead with a real typographic hierarchy over them, and put the practice's positioning in the hero rather than in the page title.
notes: Body and display both Rubik. Renders are strong and under-used. Mixed audience — clients, course applicants, job applicants — competing on one page.
